sentences.text: Revenue compounded at 24.2% a year, from $1.70 billion in FY2016 to $12.0 billion in FY2025 [F1][F10][F196].
Revenue grew 49.1% in FY2020 [D194], driven by TRIKAFTA's US launch in the fourth quarter of 2019 and KAFTRIO's EU launch in the third quarter of 2020 [P51].
Operating margin fell from 38.8% in FY2023 to -2.1% in FY2024, a 40.9pp drop, as acquired in-process R&D of $4.6 billion included $4.4 billion for Alpine [F33][F34][D408][P11].
Growth has since slowed, with revenue up 8.9% in FY2025 [D446] against a 3-year CAGR of 10.4% [D679].
TRIKAFTA/KAFTRIO reached 85.9% of revenue in FY2025, up from 62.3% in FY2020 [D529][D516].
It added 29.5pp to growth in FY2021 and 26.3pp in FY2022 but only 0.7pp in FY2025 [D519][D522][D531].
ALYFTREK, with $837.8 million of FY2025 sales, added 7.6pp to growth, more than TRIKAFTA/KAFTRIO's 0.7pp [S69][D590][D531].
Profit has lagged revenue: the 3-year operating income CAGR was -1.0% against revenue's 10.4% [D681][D679].
Diluted shares were 258.0 million in FY2025, unchanged from the prior year, so EPS growth tracked net income [X137][D459].
FY2025 operating margin of 34.8% sits above the 31.8% window median but below the 48.2% high and far above the -2.1% low [F35][D663][D662][D661].
Margin rose 36.9pp in FY2025 [D452], almost all from the residual line at +37.7pp [D468].
The residual reflects the prior-year charge of $4.6 billion of acquired in-process R&D, including $4.4 billion for Alpine, not repeating [P11][D468].
SG&A cost 1.3pp of margin, rising to 14.6% of revenue from 13.3%, and the FY2024 10-K guided to higher 2025 spend for launches [D467][D427][D384][P6].
Cost of sales was 13.8% of revenue in FY2025 [D425], with the filing citing a lower overall royalty rate for CF medicines [P4].
Operating cash flow of $3.63 billion was 0.92x net income, and free cash flow was 0.81x, against a window median of 1.07x [F85][D434][D435][D675].
The filing attributes operating cash flow primarily to income from operations of $4.17 billion [P1][F25].
Free cash flow margin was 26.6% against a 32.8% median, and capex was 3.6% of revenue and 2.09x D&A [D431][D669][D430][D436].
Net cash rose to $12.3 billion from $11.2 billion [D439][D393], and working capital rose to $7.34 billion from $6.03 billion on cash from product revenue [F175][F174][P2].
Net cash equals 102.7% of revenue, the 88th percentile among 8 biopharma peers, whose median is -50.7% [D440][D691][D692].
Buybacks were $2.02 billion in FY2025, 63.2% of free cash flow, up from $1.18 billion in FY2024 [X147][D442][X146].
Return on average equity of 22.5% is the 38th percentile of 8 peers, below their 38.7% median [D445][D695][D696].
Days inventory outstanding rose 85 days to 373 in FY2025, from 135 in FY2016, with inventory up 39.9% [R1][D444][D397][D19][D462].
The filings cited do not explain the build, and it ties up cash that could otherwise reach free cash flow [R1][D444].
Free cash flow was 0.81x net income, the 14th percentile of 7 peers, whose median is 1.11x [D435][D693][D694].
TRIKAFTA/KAFTRIO is 85.9% of revenue with growth of 0.7%, so one product's saturation now sets the top line [D529][D530].
The tax-rate swing is benign, as the FY2024 rate of 315.5% reflected non-deductible Alpine AIPR&D, and the FY2019 buyback recast touches no figure used here [R2][D390][P5][X141].
Days inventory outstanding staying above 373 days confirms the build, while a fall below FY2024's 287 days would reverse it, in the FY2026 10-K [D444][D397].
Revenue growth below 8.9% would confirm the slowdown, with TRIKAFTA/KAFTRIO growth below 0.7% as the check, in the FY2026 10-K [D446][D530].
Free cash flow to net income above the 1.07x window median would reverse the conversion gap from 0.81x, in the FY2026 10-K [D675][D435].
